The mission is complete: all four milestones are completed, all five theorems
are Proved, and the final goal has zero open leaves. All submissions are ACCEPTED:

| Proof role | Accepted artifact |
|---|---|
| Final output concentration | [ec1ba3f1](p2m:solution/ec1ba3f1-a9c1-4311-9599-d4e6a473b07d) |
| Exponential tail | [905dd122](p2m:solution/905dd122-dc0e-4f71-8beb-2b89cb191db7) |
| All-real Kearns–Saul MGF | [1c90041e](p2m:solution/1c90041e-cee7-43e8-8dd8-35618782146f) |
| Exact rescaled-error moments | [2b078813](p2m:solution/2b078813-c9cb-4a09-9230-afe8653a792a) |
| Coefficient-energy identity | [ac3f10aa](p2m:solution/ac3f10aa-19ec-4cca-936c-03bc861a7e2a) |

Scalar acceptance automatically closed the existing tail and root sketches.
The moments proof splits the finite Boolean product and inducts on dimension.
The scalar proof uses a proved log-cosh quadratic envelope, with midpoint and
probability reflection included. The complete chain has no open assumptions.

**Notation and probability model.** For fixed $c\in\mathbb R^n$, $n>0$,
independent Bernoulli($p$) drop indicators on $\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$, and
$0<p,\gamma<1$, put $H=(1-p)^{-1}\sum_jc_j(\omega_j-p)$,
$Q=\sum_jc_j^2$, $\bar c=n^{-1}\sum_jc_j$, and
$\sigma^2=n^{-1}\sum_j(c_j-\bar c)^2$.
Define $\Phi(p)=(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ off the midpoint and
$\Phi(1/2)=1/2$. The proved goal is

$$
\Pr\left\{|H|\le\frac{\sqrt{\Phi(p)}}{1-p}
\sqrt{n(\bar c^2+\sigma^2)}\sqrt{\log(2/\gamma)}\right\}\ge1-\gamma.
$$

**Formalization note:** all published types and the original model are preserved.
This is a complete proof of Appendix E.1 equation (8), with finite Chernoff and
confidence bridges to the proved scalar input. The hyperbolic scalar argument
is an alternative direct proof of Berend–Kontorovich's exact theorem; their
printed proof instead uses convexity in $p$. Moments retain empty vectors,
both probability endpoints, and arbitrary positive rescaling. Every final
axiom audit contains only standard Lean axioms.

**Sources:** Deng et al., *DARE the Extreme*,
[arXiv:2410.09344v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2), Section 3.2,
PDF p. 5 equation (2); Appendix E.1 PDF p. 29, initial unnumbered moments,
Theorem E.1 equations (6)–(7); PDF p. 30, tail before equation (8) and
equation (8); PDF p. 31, unnumbered energy identity; Appendix E.2 PDF p. 31,
initial unnumbered rescaling identity. Berend–Kontorovich,
*On the Concentration of the Missing Mass*,
[arXiv:1210.3248v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1210.3248v1), Section 3,
PDF p. 3, Lemma 3 and Theorem 4 equation (6), proof PDF pp. 3–4.

Accepted [tail sketch 905dd122](p2m:sketch/905dd122-dc0e-4f71-8beb-2b89cb191db7)
reduces [DAREx.DAREExponentialTail](p2m:theorem/d7ac7bac-7a7c-4084-b4a8-4584aa769192)
to the existing [DAREx.KearnsSaulMGF](p2m:theorem/d384aa62-fd26-4739-9089-8a6a761e66f5).
The root's live open frontier is now exactly this scalar theorem. Root and tail
remain Open until that input is proved.

Direct [proof ac3f10aa](p2m:solution/ac3f10aa-19ec-4cca-936c-03bc861a7e2a)
is also ACCEPTED: [DAREx.CoefficientEnergyIdentity](p2m:theorem/19fbf6ac-3926-4a48-abe1-6c3f27baf80a)
now reads Proved, with no open theorem dependencies.

**Notation and probability model.** Fix $c\in\mathbb R^n$, $0<p<1$, and
independent Bernoulli($p$) drop indicators on $\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$.
Put $Q=\sum_jc_j^2$ and $H=(1-p)^{-1}\sum_jc_j(\omega_j-p)$.
Define $\Phi(p)=(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ away from $p=1/2$ and
$\Phi(1/2)=1/2$. The tail solution proves product factorization,
$\mathbb E e^{sH}\le e^{\Phi(p)Qs^2/(4(1-p)^2)}$, and both finite

$\Pr(|H|>t)\le2e^{-t^2(1-p)^2/(\Phi(p)Q)}$.
It needs the scalar MGF at every real argument, including negative ones.
For $n>0$, the direct identity proof establishes
$Q=n(\bar c^2+\sigma^2)$, where $\bar c=n^{-1}\sum_jc_j$ and
$\sigma^2=n^{-1}\sum_j(c_j-\bar c)^2$.

**Formalization note:** the tail is a formal Lean bridge with one explicit
scalar analytic child; the energy identity is direct source algebra.

Accepted [proof-sketch ec1ba3f1](p2m:sketch/ec1ba3f1-a9c1-4311-9599-d4e6a473b07d)

**Notation and probability model.** For fixed $c\in\mathbb R^n$, $n>0$, independent Bernoulli($p$) drop masks

**Formalization note:** formal Lean bridge, with exact target type and one

submissions.explanation:
For every real coefficient vector $c\in\mathbb R^n$ with $n>0$,

$$\sum_jc_j^2=n(\bar c^2+\sigma^2).$$

**Notation.** Here $n$ is the number of coordinates,
$\bar c=n^{-1}\sum_jc_j$ is their empirical mean, and
$\sigma^2=n^{-1}\sum_j(c_j-\bar c)^2$ is their empirical variance,
with denominator $n$. The coefficients are fixed and may be signed or zero.
The identity supplies coefficient energy for the DARE Bernoulli($p$)
pruning model, where $\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$ is the mask space and $p$ is the
drop probability; the equality itself is deterministic.

Expanding the squared deviations gives

$$
\sum_j(c_j-\bar c)^2
=\sum_jc_j^2-2\bar c\sum_jc_j+n\bar c^2
=\sum_jc_j^2-n\bar c^2,
$$

where $\sum_jc_j=n\bar c$ and $n\ne0$ follow from the mean definition
and the positive-dimension hypothesis. Dividing by $n$ and rearranging gives
the claimed identity. The submitted proof carries out these finite-sum
expansions and field equalities directly.

**Formalization note:** direct source algebraic identity. The top-level
`theorem solution` has exactly the existing milestone's complete type.
There are no imported open theorems or analytic assumptions; singleton,
zero, and signed coefficient vectors are all included.

**Source:** Deng et al., *DARE the Extreme: Revisiting Delta-Parameter
Pruning For Fine-Tuned Models*, ICLR 2025,
[arXiv:2410.09344v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2), Appendix E.1,
PDF p. 31, unnumbered coefficient-energy identity immediately after the
Berend–Kontorovich paragraph; Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, Theorem 3.1 statistical
definitions. This identity supplies the empirical-statistics rewrite of
Appendix E.1, PDF p. 30, equation (8).

import Definitions.Def_DAREx_Model
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators
open DAREx

-- Deng et al., Appendix E.1, PDF p. 31, unnumbered coefficient-energy identity.
theorem solution :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ), 0 < n →
      energy c = (n : ℝ) * (empiricalMean c ^ 2 + empiricalVariance c) := by
  intro n c hn
  have hn' : (n : ℝ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.ne_of_gt hn)
  unfold empiricalVariance empiricalMean coefficientSum energy
  simp_rw [sub_sq, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_sub_distrib,
    ← Finset.sum_mul, ← Finset.mul_sum]
  simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
  field_simp
  ring

theorem.formal_statement:
namespace DAREx
theorem CoefficientEnergyIdentity :
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ), 0 < n →
    energy c = (n : ℝ) * (empiricalMean c ^ 2 + empiricalVariance c) := by sorry
end DAREx
theorem.natural_language_statement:
**Notation.** The fixed-cardinality coordinate set is $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with $n=|I|$; $c_j$ are real coefficients, $Q$ their squared energy, and $\bar c,\sigma^2$ their empirical statistics. For $n>0$ and any deterministic real coefficient vector $c\in\mathbb R^n$, define $Q=\sum_jc_j^2$, $\bar c=n^{-1}\sum_jc_j$, and $\sigma^2=n^{-1}\sum_j(c_j-\bar c)^2$. Then $$Q=n(\bar c^2+\sigma^2).$$ These are statistics over coordinates, not moments over random pruning. **Formalization note:** direct algebraic identity used in the source; no coefficient sign assumption.

**Source:** Deng et al., DARE the Extreme: Revisiting Delta-Parameter Pruning For Fine-Tuned Models, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.09344v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2, Appendix E.1, PDF p. 31, unnumbered identity immediately after the Berend–Kontorovich paragraph; Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, Theorem 3.1 definitions.

readback.readback: This open theorem asserts that, for every natural number $n$ and every real coefficient family $c:I_n\to\mathbb R$, where $I_n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, if $0<n$, then $\sum_{j\in I_n}c_j^2=n\bigl(\bar c^{\,2}+s_c^2\bigr)$, where $\bar c=(\sum_{j\in I_n}c_j)/n$ and $s_c^2=(\sum_{j\in I_n}(c_j-\bar c)^2)/n$, and $n$ in real arithmetic is the corresponding real number. The empirical variance has denominator $n$, not $n-1$. There is no sign, nonzero, normalization, or probabilistic hypothesis on the coefficients. The case $n=0$ is excluded by the positive-size hypothesis; $n=1$ and the identically zero coefficient family are included, with variance $0$ in the singleton case. The supplied proof slot is a placeholder; no completed proof is supplied.

milestones.milestone_description:
For any $n\ge0$, fixed coefficients $c_j\in\mathbb R$, $0\le p\le1$, and $q>0$, draw independent Bernoulli($p$) drop indicators $\omega_j$. Put $H_q=\sum_jc_j(1-(1-\omega_j)/q)$, $S=\sum_jc_j$, $Q=\sum_jc_j^2$, and $b_q=(1-(1-p)/q)S$. Then $$\mathbb EH_q=b_q,\qquad\mathbb E(H_q-b_q)^2=\frac{p(1-p)}{q^2}Q,$$ $$\mathbb EH_q^2=b_q^2+\frac{p(1-p)}{q^2}Q.$$ Expectations are finite product-mask sums. **Formalization note:** paper-derived extension of the DARE moment calculation to the general $1/q$ rescaling model; this does not assert the optimizer or tail formula later printed in Appendix E.2. Empty vectors and deterministic endpoint masks are included.

Source: Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, equation (2); Appendix E.1, PDF p. 29, initial unnumbered mean/variance calculations; Appendix E.2, PDF p. 31, initial unnumbered general-rescaling identity. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2

submissions.explanation:
For every fixed $c\in\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge0$, $0\le p\le1$, and $q>0$,
the rescaled pruning error has exact bias, variance, and mean square:

$$
\mathbb E H_q=b_q,\qquad
\mathbb E(H_q-b_q)^2=\frac{p(1-p)}{q^2}Q,\qquad
\mathbb E H_q^2=b_q^2+\frac{p(1-p)}{q^2}Q.
$$

**Notation and probability model.** Here $p$ is the drop probability,
$\omega\in\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$ has independent Bernoulli($p$) coordinates,
and its mass is the product of $p$ at a dropped coordinate and $1-p$
at a surviving coordinate. The rescaling denominator is $q$,
$H_q=\sum_j(c_j-(1-\omega_j)c_j/q)$,
$S=\sum_jc_j$, $Q=\sum_jc_j^2$, and
$b_q=(1-(1-p)/q)S$. Expectations are the model's finite weighted sums.

The proof splits a mask in dimension $n+1$ into its first Boolean coordinate
and its remaining $n$ coordinates. The product mass therefore gives
$(1-p)$ times the surviving-coordinate conditional expectation plus $p$
times the dropped-coordinate conditional expectation. At the first
coordinate, the two error increments are $c_0-c_0/q$ and $c_0$.

Induction simultaneously computes the first and raw second moments. Adding
an increment $a$ to the remaining error $X$ uses
$\mathbb E(a+X)^2=a^2+2a\mathbb EX+\mathbb EX^2$.
The weighted first-coordinate variance is exactly
$p(1-p)c_0^2/q^2$, so summing the coordinate contributions yields the
displayed raw second moment. Expanding $(H_q-b_q)^2$ and using the proved
first moment yields the centered second moment. The empty vector starts
the induction with zero error; both deterministic probability endpoints
are included without a limiting argument.

**Formalization note:** paper-derived extension of the source's finite DARE
moment calculation to the arbitrary positive $1/q$ rescaling model.
The submitted `theorem solution` matches the complete existing target type.
The proof establishes the finite product calculation directly and imports
no open theorem. It asserts neither an optimal choice of $q$ nor an
additional concentration formula.

**Source:** Deng et al., *DARE the Extreme: Revisiting Delta-Parameter
Pruning For Fine-Tuned Models*, ICLR 2025,
[arXiv:2410.09344v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2), Section 3.2,
PDF p. 5, equation (2); Appendix E.1, PDF p. 29, initial unnumbered
mean and variance calculations; Appendix E.2, PDF p. 31, initial unnumbered
general-rescaling identity. The moment displays have no equation numbers.

import Definitions.Def_DAREx_Model
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Tuple.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators
open DAREx

-- Fin.consEquiv and the finite product/sum APIs supply the independence calculation.
private lemma mean_cons {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ) (f : Mask (n + 1) → ℝ) :
    mean p f = (1 - p) * mean p (fun ω ↦ f (Fin.cons false ω)) +
      p * mean p (fun ω ↦ f (Fin.cons true ω)) := by
  unfold mean
  rw [← (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) ↦ Bool)).sum_comp
    (fun ω ↦ maskMass p ω * f ω)]
  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  simp [maskMass, Fin.prod_univ_succ, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]
  exact add_comm _ _

private lemma mean_const {n : ℕ} (p a : ℝ) :
    mean p (fun _ : Mask n ↦ a) = a := by
  unfold mean
  rw [← Finset.sum_mul, maskMass_sum, one_mul]

private lemma mean_add {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ) (f g : Mask n → ℝ) :
    mean p (fun ω ↦ f ω + g ω) = mean p f + mean p g := by
  simp [mean, mul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib]

private lemma mean_mul {n : ℕ} (p a : ℝ) (f : Mask n → ℝ) :
    mean p (fun ω ↦ a * f ω) = a * mean p f := by
  simp [mean, Finset.mul_sum, mul_left_comm]

private lemma mean_shift_sq {n : ℕ} (p a : ℝ) (f : Mask n → ℝ) :
    mean p (fun ω ↦ (a + f ω) ^ 2) =
      a ^ 2 + 2 * a * mean p f + mean p (fun ω ↦ f ω ^ 2) := by
  have h : (fun ω ↦ (a + f ω) ^ 2) =
      (fun ω ↦ (a ^ 2 + (2 * a) * f ω) + f ω ^ 2) := by
    funext ω
    ring
  rw [h, mean_add, mean_add, mean_const, mean_mul]

private lemma error_cons {n : ℕ} (q : ℝ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)
    (b : Bool) (ω : Mask n) :
    outputError q c (Fin.cons b ω) =
      (c 0 - (if b then 0 else c 0 / q)) + outputError q (fun j ↦ c j.succ) ω := by
  simp [outputError, Fin.sum_univ_succ]
  ring

private lemma bias_cons {n : ℕ} (p q : ℝ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) :
    outputBias p q c = (1 - (1 - p) / q) * c 0 +
      outputBias p q (fun j ↦ c j.succ) := by
  simp [outputBias, coefficientSum, Fin.sum_univ_succ, mul_add]

private lemma energy_cons {n : ℕ} (c : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) :
    energy c = c 0 ^ 2 + energy (fun j ↦ c j.succ) := by
  simp [energy, Fin.sum_univ_succ]

private lemma raw_moments (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p q : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    mean p (outputError q c) = outputBias p q c ∧
    mean p (fun ω ↦ outputError q c ω ^ 2) =
      outputBias p q c ^ 2 + p * (1 - p) / q ^ 2 * energy c := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [outputError, outputBias, coefficientSum, energy, mean]
  | succ n ih =>
    obtain ⟨hfirst, hsecond⟩ := ih (fun j ↦ c j.succ)
    constructor
    · rw [mean_cons, bias_cons]
      simp_rw [error_cons]
      simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, if_true, sub_zero]
      rw [mean_add, mean_add, mean_const, mean_const, hfirst]
      field_simp
      ring
    · rw [mean_cons, bias_cons, energy_cons]
      simp_rw [error_cons]
      simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, if_true, sub_zero]
      rw [mean_shift_sq, mean_shift_sq, hfirst, hsecond]
      field_simp
      ring

theorem solution :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p q : ℝ), 0 ≤ p → p ≤ 1 → 0 < q →
      mean p (outputError q c) = outputBias p q c ∧
      mean p (fun ω ↦ (outputError q c ω - outputBias p q c) ^ 2) =
        p * (1 - p) / q ^ 2 * energy c ∧
      mean p (fun ω ↦ outputError q c ω ^ 2) =
        outputBias p q c ^ 2 + p * (1 - p) / q ^ 2 * energy c := by
  intro n c p q _hp _hp' hq
  obtain ⟨hfirst, hsecond⟩ := raw_moments n c p q hq
  refine ⟨hfirst, ?_, hsecond⟩
  have h : (fun ω ↦ (outputError q c ω - outputBias p q c) ^ 2) =
      (fun ω ↦ (-outputBias p q c + outputError q c ω) ^ 2) := by
    funext ω
    ring
  rw [h, mean_shift_sq, hfirst, hsecond]
  ring

theorem.formal_statement:
namespace DAREx
theorem RescaledErrorMoments :
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p q : ℝ), 0 ≤ p → p ≤ 1 → 0 < q →
    mean p (outputError q c) = outputBias p q c ∧
    mean p (fun ω ↦ (outputError q c ω - outputBias p q c) ^ 2) =
      p * (1 - p) / q ^ 2 * energy c ∧
    mean p (fun ω ↦ outputError q c ω ^ 2) =
      outputBias p q c ^ 2 + p * (1 - p) / q ^ 2 * energy c := by sorry
end DAREx
theorem.natural_language_statement:
**Notation.** $\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$ is the finite space of Bernoulli drop masks; $n$ is the number of coordinates and $p$ is the drop probability. Coefficients are fixed before drawing the mask. For any $n\ge0$, fixed coefficients $c_j\in\mathbb R$, $0\le p\le1$, and $q>0$, draw independent Bernoulli($p$) drop indicators $\omega_j$. Put $H_q=\sum_jc_j(1-(1-\omega_j)/q)$, $S=\sum_jc_j$, $Q=\sum_jc_j^2$, and $b_q=(1-(1-p)/q)S$. Then $$\mathbb EH_q=b_q,\qquad\mathbb E(H_q-b_q)^2=\frac{p(1-p)}{q^2}Q,$$ $$\mathbb EH_q^2=b_q^2+\frac{p(1-p)}{q^2}Q.$$ Expectations are finite product-mask sums. **Formalization note:** paper-derived extension of the DARE moment calculation to the general $1/q$ rescaling model; this does not assert the optimizer or tail formula later printed in Appendix E.2. Empty vectors and deterministic endpoint masks are included.

**Source:** Deng et al., DARE the Extreme: Revisiting Delta-Parameter Pruning For Fine-Tuned Models, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.09344v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2, Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, equation (2); Appendix E.1, PDF p. 29, initial unnumbered mean/variance calculations; Appendix E.2, PDF p. 31, initial unnumbered general-rescaling identity.

readback.readback: This open theorem asserts that, for every natural number $n$, every real coefficient family $c:I_n\to\mathbb R$ with $I_n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and every pair of real numbers $p,q$ satisfying $0\le p\le1$ and $0<q$, the following three equalities hold simultaneously. Let $\Omega_n=\{\mathsf{false},\mathsf{true}\}^{I_n}$, assign each mask weight $w_p(\omega)=\prod_{j\in I_n}a_p(\omega_j)$ with $a_p(\mathsf{true})=p$ and $a_p(\mathsf{false})=1-p$, and define $\mathcal M_p(f)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_n}w_p(\omega)f(\omega)$. These are the weights of independent Boolean coordinates that are true with probability $p$. Put $C=\sum_{j\in I_n}c_j$, $V=\sum_{j\in I_n}c_j^2$, $E(\omega)=\sum_{j\in I_n}(c_j-h_j(\omega_j))$, where $h_j(\mathsf{true})=0$ and $h_j(\mathsf{false})=c_j/q$, and $b=(1-(1-p)/q)C$. Then $\mathcal M_p(E)=b$, $\mathcal M_p(\omega\mapsto(E(\omega)-b)^2)=p(1-p)V/q^2$, and $\mathcal M_p(\omega\mapsto E(\omega)^2)=b^2+p(1-p)V/q^2$. The parameter $q$ can be any positive real number and is not required to equal $1-p$ or to be at most $1$; no nonzero-energy or positive-size assumption is imposed. The endpoints $p=0$ and $p=1$ are included: the product distribution is then deterministic and the claimed centered second moment is $0$. The empty case $n=0$ is included, has exactly one mask of weight $1$, and has $C=V=E=b=0$, so all three equalities read $0=0$; the zero coefficient family is also included for every $n$. The supplied proof slot is a placeholder; no completed proof is supplied.

milestones.milestone_description:
For $0<p<1$, let $\Phi(p)=(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ when $p\ne1/2$, and $\Phi(1/2)=1/2$. Then $0<\Phi(p)\le1/2$, and for every real $t$, $$ (1-p)e^{-tp}+pe^{t(1-p)}\le\exp(\Phi(p)t^2/4).$$ The left side is the exponential moment of a centered Bernoulli($p$) variable. Both signs of $t$ are part of the conclusion. **Formalization note:** explicitly sourced external analytic input, specialized to the open probability interval needed by DARE, together with the source's coefficient bound. The half-probability value is the removable-singularity extension in the proof of Berend–Kontorovich Theorem 4. It is not the one-sided refinement in Lemma 5.

Source: Appendix E.1, PDF p. 29, Theorem E.1 and equations (6)–(7); PDF p. 30, bounds on Phi following equation (8). Berend and Kontorovich, On the Concentration of the Missing Mass, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1210.3248v1, Section 3, PDF p. 3, Theorem 4, equation (6), proof PDF pp. 3–4. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2

submissions.explanation:
For $0<p<1$, define $\Phi(p)=(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ when $p\ne1/2$,
and $\Phi(1/2)=1/2$. We prove

$$
0<\Phi(p)\le\frac12,\qquad
(1-p)e^{-pt}+pe^{(1-p)t}\le e^{\Phi(p)t^2/4}
\quad\text{for every }t\in\mathbb R.
$$

**Notation and probability model.** The parameter $p$ is the Bernoulli drop
probability. The left side is $\mathbb E e^{t(B-p)}$ for $B\in\{0,1\}$
with $\Pr(B=1)=p$. In the DARE application, the mask space
$\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$ has independent copies of $B$, and the fixed coefficient
vector $c\in\mathbb R^n$ may have either sign. This is why both signs of
the scalar parameter $t$ must be covered.

We give an alternative direct analytic proof of the exact Kearns–Saul
statement. First, the function $r(x)=\tanh(x)/x$ decreases on $x>0$.
Writing it as $\sinh(x)/(x\cosh(x))$ gives

$$r'(x)=\frac{x-\sinh(x)\cosh(x)}{(x\cosh(x))^2}\le0,$$

because $\sinh(2x)=2\sinh(x)\cosh(x)\ge2x$ for $x\ge0$.
For $a>0$, the differentiable even function
$F_a(x)=\log\cosh x-\tanh(a)x^2/(2a)$ has derivative
$\tanh x-r(a)x$. It is nonnegative on $(0,a)$ and nonpositive on
$(a,\infty)$. Continuity supplies the interval endpoints, and evenness
therefore yields, for every real $x$,

$$
\log\cosh x\le\log\cosh a+
\frac{\tanh a}{2a}(x^2-a^2).
$$

Suppose first $p<1/2$. Put $\delta=1-2p\in(0,1)$ and
$a=\operatorname{artanh}\delta>0$. Then
$\tanh a=\delta$, $2a=\log((1-p)/p)$, and $\Phi(p)=\delta/(2a)$.
The exact exponential-moment identity is

$$
(1-p)e^{-pt}+pe^{(1-p)t}
=e^{\delta t/2}\frac{\cosh(t/2-a)}{\cosh a}.
$$

Apply the envelope at $x=t/2-a$ and take the logarithm of this positive
expression. Its upper bound simplifies to
$\delta t/2+\delta((t/2-a)^2-a^2)/(2a)
=\delta t^2/(8a)=\Phi(p)t^2/4$.
Exponentiating proves the asserted moment inequality for every real $t$.
Positivity of $\Phi$ is immediate in this branch. The derivative of
$x\cosh x-\sinh x$ is $x\sinh x\ge0$ on $x\ge0$, and its value at zero
is zero. Thus $\tanh a\le a$ and $\Phi(p)\le1/2$.

For $p>1/2$, use $q=1-p<1/2$, the exact symmetry
$\Phi(q)=\Phi(p)$, and $M_p(t)=M_q(-t)$. At $p=1/2$ the moment is
$\cosh(t/2)\le e^{t^2/8}$, the classical hyperbolic estimate proved in
Mathlib by comparing power series. This agrees with the defined midpoint
value of $\Phi$.

**Formalization note:** direct analytic proof of the existing source-backed
external theorem, with the coefficient bounds required by DARE. The
hyperbolic route above is an alternative proof; Berend–Kontorovich's printed
proof uses convexity in $p$. Every support lemma is proved and included in
the standalone submitted file. The complete `theorem solution` type is
unchanged, and there are no open theorem imports or added assumptions.

**Sources:** Berend and Kontorovich, *On the Concentration of the Missing Mass*,
[arXiv:1210.3248v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1210.3248v1), Section 3, PDF p. 3,
Lemma 3 and Theorem 4, equation (6), proof on PDF pp. 3–4. The all-real
Kearns–Saul result, rather than the one-sided Lemma 5, is used. Deng et al.,
*DARE the Extreme*, [arXiv:2410.09344v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2),
Appendix E.1, PDF p. 29, Theorem E.1, equations (6)–(7); PDF p. 30,
coefficient bounds after equation (8).

import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.DerivHyp
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Series
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Deriv
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp

-- Inlined from Definitions/DAREx/Hyperbolic.lean.
/-! Elementary hyperbolic inequalities for the sharp Kearns--Saul bound.
The log-cosh quadratic envelope is equivalent to the analytic inequality in
Berend--Kontorovich, arXiv:1210.3248v1, Section 3, PDF pp. 3--4,
Theorem 4, equation (6). The proof here uses a hyperbolic reformulation.
-/

noncomputable section
open Set

namespace DAREx

private lemma sinh_ratio_eq (x : ℝ) :
    Real.sinh x / (x * Real.cosh x) = Real.tanh x / x := by
  rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh, div_div]
  congr 1
  ring

private lemma hasDerivAt_sinh_ratio (x : ℝ) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    HasDerivAt (fun y ↦ Real.sinh y / (y * Real.cosh y))
      ((x - Real.sinh x * Real.cosh x) / (x * Real.cosh x) ^ 2) x := by
  convert (Real.hasDerivAt_sinh x).div
    ((hasDerivAt_id x).mul (Real.hasDerivAt_cosh x))
    (mul_ne_zero hx (Real.cosh_pos x).ne') using 1
  congr 1
  have h := congrArg (fun z : ℝ ↦ x * z) (Real.cosh_sq_sub_sinh_sq x)
  dsimp only [Pi.mul_apply, id] at h ⊢
  nlinarith

lemma antitoneOn_tanh_div : AntitoneOn (fun x : ℝ ↦ Real.tanh x / x) (Ioi 0) := by
  have hratio : AntitoneOn (fun x : ℝ ↦ Real.sinh x / (x * Real.cosh x)) (Ioi 0) := by
    apply antitoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonpos (convex_Ioi 0)
    · apply ContinuousOn.div Real.continuous_sinh.continuousOn
        (continuous_id.mul Real.continuous_cosh).continuousOn
      intro x hx
      exact mul_ne_zero (ne_of_gt hx) (Real.cosh_pos x).ne'
    · intro x hx
      rw [interior_Ioi] at hx
      exact (hasDerivAt_sinh_ratio x (ne_of_gt hx)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro x hx
      rw [interior_Ioi] at hx
      change 0 < x at hx
      apply div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg _ (sq_nonneg _)
      have h := Real.self_le_sinh_iff.mpr (show 0 ≤ 2 * x by linarith)
      rw [Real.sinh_two_mul] at h
      linarith
  simpa only [sinh_ratio_eq] using hratio

lemma log_cosh_le_half_sq (x : ℝ) : Real.log (Real.cosh x) ≤ x ^ 2 / 2 := by
  exact (Real.log_le_iff_le_exp (Real.cosh_pos x)).mpr (Real.cosh_le_exp_half_sq x)

private lemma hasDerivAt_log_cosh_quadratic (a x : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    HasDerivAt (fun y ↦ Real.log (Real.cosh y) -
      (Real.tanh a / (2 * a)) * y ^ 2)
      (Real.tanh x - (Real.tanh a / a) * x) x := by
  convert ((Real.hasDerivAt_cosh x).log (Real.cosh_pos x).ne').sub
    (((hasDerivAt_id x).pow 2).const_mul (Real.tanh a / (2 * a))) using 1
  rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh]
  dsimp only [id]
  field_simp
  ring

lemma log_cosh_quadratic_envelope {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (x : ℝ) :
    Real.log (Real.cosh x) ≤ Real.log (Real.cosh a) +
      (Real.tanh a / (2 * a)) * (x ^ 2 - a ^ 2) := by
  let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun y ↦ Real.log (Real.cosh y) -
    (Real.tanh a / (2 * a)) * y ^ 2
  have hf (y : ℝ) : HasDerivAt f (Real.tanh y - (Real.tanh a / a) * y) y :=
    hasDerivAt_log_cosh_quadratic a y ha.ne'
  have hdiff : Differentiable ℝ f := fun y ↦ (hf y).differentiableAt
  have hmono : MonotoneOn f (Icc 0 a) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg (convex_Icc 0 a) hdiff.continuous.continuousOn
      hdiff.differentiableOn
    intro y hy
    rw [interior_Icc, mem_Ioo] at hy
    rw [(hf y).deriv]
    have h := antitoneOn_tanh_div hy.1 ha hy.2.le
    exact sub_nonneg.mpr ((le_div_iff₀ hy.1).mp h)
  have hanti : AntitoneOn f (Ici a) := by
    apply antitoneOn_of_deriv_nonpos (convex_Ici a) hdiff.continuous.continuousOn
      hdiff.differentiableOn
    intro y hy
    rw [interior_Ici, mem_Ioi] at hy
    rw [(hf y).deriv]
    have hy0 := ha.trans hy
    have h := antitoneOn_tanh_div ha hy0 hy.le
    exact sub_nonpos.mpr ((div_le_iff₀ hy0).mp h)
  have hmax : f |x| ≤ f a := by
    by_cases hxa : |x| ≤ a
    · exact hmono ⟨abs_nonneg x, hxa⟩ ⟨ha.le, le_rfl⟩ hxa
    · exact hanti (mem_Ici.mpr (le_refl a))
        (show |x| ∈ Ici a from le_of_not_ge hxa) (le_of_not_ge hxa)
  dsimp only [f] at hmax
  rw [Real.cosh_abs, sq_abs] at hmax
  nlinarith

lemma tanh_le_self {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) : Real.tanh a ≤ a := by
  have hder (x : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (fun y ↦ y * Real.cosh y - Real.sinh y)
      (x * Real.sinh x) x := by
    convert ((hasDerivAt_id x).mul (Real.hasDerivAt_cosh x)).sub
      (Real.hasDerivAt_sinh x) using 1
    dsimp only [id]
    ring
  have hdiff : Differentiable ℝ (fun y ↦ y * Real.cosh y - Real.sinh y) :=
    fun x ↦ (hder x).differentiableAt
  have hmono : MonotoneOn (fun y ↦ y * Real.cosh y - Real.sinh y) (Ici 0) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg (convex_Ici 0) hdiff.continuous.continuousOn
      hdiff.differentiableOn
    intro x hx
    rw [interior_Ici, mem_Ioi] at hx
    rw [(hder x).deriv]
    exact mul_nonneg hx.le (Real.sinh_nonneg_iff.mpr hx.le)
  have h := hmono (mem_Ici.mpr (le_refl (0 : ℝ))) ha ha
  simp only [Real.cosh_zero, Real.sinh_zero, zero_mul, sub_zero] at h
  rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh, div_le_iff₀ (Real.cosh_pos a)]
  linarith

end DAREx

-- Inlined from Definitions/DAREx/KearnsSaul.lean.
noncomputable section

namespace DAREx

lemma ks_phi_symmetry {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p < 1) :
    phi (1 - p) = phi p := by
  unfold phi
  by_cases hh : p = 1 / 2
  · subst p
    norm_num
  · have hh' : 1 - p ≠ 1 / 2 := by
      intro h
      apply hh
      linarith
    rw [if_neg hh, if_neg hh']
    have hratio : (1 - (1 - p)) / (1 - p) = ((1 - p) / p)⁻¹ := by
      field_simp
      ring
    rw [hratio, Real.log_inv]
    ring

lemma ks_parameter {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hlow : p < 1 / 2) :
    0 < Real.artanh (1 - 2 * p) ∧
    Real.tanh (Real.artanh (1 - 2 * p)) = 1 - 2 * p ∧
    2 * Real.artanh (1 - 2 * p) = Real.log ((1 - p) / p) := by
  have hδ : 1 - 2 * p ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 := ⟨by linarith, by linarith⟩
  have hδ' : 1 - 2 * p ∈ Set.Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1 := ⟨by linarith [hδ.1], hδ.2⟩
  refine ⟨Real.artanh_pos hδ, Real.tanh_artanh hδ', ?_⟩
  rw [Real.artanh_eq_half_log ⟨hδ'.1.le, hδ'.2.le⟩]
  have hr : (1 + (1 - 2 * p)) / (1 - (1 - 2 * p)) = (1 - p) / p := by
    field_simp
    ring
  rw [hr]
  ring

lemma ks_mgf_hyperbolic (p t a : ℝ) (ha : Real.tanh a = 1 - 2 * p) :
    (1 - p) * Real.exp (-t * p) + p * Real.exp (t * (1 - p)) =
      Real.exp ((1 - 2 * p) * t / 2) * Real.cosh (t / 2 - a) / Real.cosh a := by
  have hc : Real.cosh a ≠ 0 := (Real.cosh_pos a).ne'
  have hs : Real.sinh a = (1 - 2 * p) * Real.cosh a := by
    rw [Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh] at ha
    exact (div_eq_iff hc).1 ha
  have he₁ : Real.exp (-t * p) =
      Real.exp ((1 - 2 * p) * t / 2) * Real.exp (-(t / 2)) := by
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  have he₂ : Real.exp (t * (1 - p)) =
      Real.exp ((1 - 2 * p) * t / 2) * Real.exp (t / 2) := by
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  rw [he₁, he₂, Real.cosh_sub, hs, Real.cosh_eq (t / 2), Real.sinh_eq (t / 2)]
  field_simp
  ring

lemma ks_phi_parameter {p : ℝ} (hlow : p < 1 / 2) (a : ℝ)
    (hδ : Real.tanh a = 1 - 2 * p)
    (hlog : 2 * a = Real.log ((1 - p) / p)) :
    phi p = Real.tanh a / (2 * a) := by
  unfold phi
  rw [if_neg (ne_of_lt hlow), ← hlog, hδ]

lemma ks_mgf_low_from_envelope {p a : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hlow : p < 1 / 2)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hδ : Real.tanh a = 1 - 2 * p)
    (hlog : 2 * a = Real.log ((1 - p) / p))
    (henv : ∀ x : ℝ, Real.log (Real.cosh x) ≤ Real.log (Real.cosh a) +
      Real.tanh a / (2 * a) * (x ^ 2 - a ^ 2)) (t : ℝ) :
    (1 - p) * Real.exp (-t * p) + p * Real.exp (t * (1 - p)) ≤
      Real.exp (phi p * t ^ 2 / 4) := by
  have hc : Real.cosh a ≠ 0 := (Real.cosh_pos a).ne'
  have hm : 0 < (1 - p) * Real.exp (-t * p) + p * Real.exp (t * (1 - p)) :=
    add_pos (mul_pos (by linarith) (Real.exp_pos _)) (mul_pos hp (Real.exp_pos _))
  apply (Real.log_le_iff_le_exp hm).1
  rw [ks_mgf_hyperbolic p t a hδ,
    Real.log_div (mul_ne_zero (Real.exp_ne_zero _) (Real.cosh_pos _).ne') hc,
    Real.log_mul (Real.exp_ne_zero _) (Real.cosh_pos _).ne', Real.log_exp]
  calc
    _ ≤ (1 - 2 * p) * t / 2 +
        (Real.log (Real.cosh a) + Real.tanh a / (2 * a) *
          ((t / 2 - a) ^ 2 - a ^ 2)) - Real.log (Real.cosh a) := by
      linarith [henv (t / 2 - a)]
    _ = phi p * t ^ 2 / 4 := by
      rw [ks_phi_parameter hlow a hδ hlog, hδ]
      field_simp
      ring

lemma kearns_saul_low {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hlow : p < 1 / 2) :
    0 < phi p ∧ phi p ≤ 1 / 2 ∧
    ∀ t : ℝ, (1 - p) * Real.exp (-t * p) + p * Real.exp (t * (1 - p)) ≤
      Real.exp (phi p * t ^ 2 / 4) := by
  let a := Real.artanh (1 - 2 * p)
  obtain ⟨ha, hδ, hlog⟩ := ks_parameter hp hlow
  have hphi := ks_phi_parameter hlow a hδ hlog
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [hphi, hδ]
    exact div_pos (by linarith) (mul_pos (by norm_num) ha)
  · rw [hphi]
    apply (div_le_iff₀ (mul_pos (by norm_num) ha)).2
    have h := tanh_le_self ha.le
    nlinarith
  · exact ks_mgf_low_from_envelope hp hlow ha hδ hlog
      (log_cosh_quadratic_envelope ha)

-- Alternative direct analytic proof of Berend–Kontorovich, Section 3,
-- PDF p. 3, Theorem 4 (6); the midpoint uses the paper's Lemma 3.
theorem kearns_saul_mgf (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p < 1) :
    0 < phi p ∧ phi p ≤ 1 / 2 ∧
    ∀ t : ℝ, (1 - p) * Real.exp (-t * p) + p * Real.exp (t * (1 - p)) ≤
      Real.exp (phi p * t ^ 2 / 4) := by
  rcases lt_trichotomy p (1 / 2) with hlow | rfl | hhigh
  · exact kearns_saul_low hp hlow
  · refine ⟨by norm_num [phi], by norm_num [phi], ?_⟩
    intro t
    have he₁ : -t * (1 / 2) = -(t / 2) := by ring
    have he₂ : t * (1 - 1 / 2) = t / 2 := by ring
    calc
      _ = Real.cosh (t / 2) := by
        rw [he₁, he₂, Real.cosh_eq]
        ring
      _ ≤ Real.exp ((t / 2) ^ 2 / 2) := Real.cosh_le_exp_half_sq _
      _ = _ := by
        apply congrArg Real.exp
        norm_num [phi]
        ring
  · have hq : 0 < 1 - p := by linarith
    have hq' : 1 - p < 1 / 2 := by linarith
    obtain ⟨hpos, hbound, hmgf⟩ := kearns_saul_low hq hq'
    rw [ks_phi_symmetry hp hp'] at hpos hbound hmgf
    refine ⟨hpos, hbound, ?_⟩
    intro t
    simpa only [sub_sub_cancel, neg_neg, neg_mul, neg_sq, add_comm] using hmgf (-t)

end DAREx

readback.readback: This open theorem asserts that, for every real number $p$ satisfying $0<p<1$, the explicitly defined scalar $\phi(p)$ satisfies both $0<\phi(p)$ and $\phi(p)\le\tfrac12$, and, for every real number $t$, $(1-p)\exp(-tp)+p\exp(t(1-p))\le\exp(\phi(p)t^2/4)$. Here $\phi(p)=\tfrac12$ when $p=\tfrac12$, and $\phi(p)=(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ otherwise; $\log$ is the real logarithm and $\exp$ is the real exponential. The left-hand side is explicitly the two-point weighted sum for a variable taking the centered values $-p$ and $1-p$ with weights $1-p$ and $p$, respectively; no unspecified random variable or probability-space assumption occurs. The two bounds on $\phi(p)$ are conclusions in conjunction with the exponential inequality, not assumptions. The parameter $t$ is unrestricted and may be negative, zero, or positive; at $t=0$ the exponential inequality is $1\le1$. The midpoint $p=\tfrac12$ is included using its designated value of $\phi$, giving $\tfrac12\exp(-t/2)+\tfrac12\exp(t/2)\le\exp(t^2/8)$; the endpoints $p=0$ and $p=1$ are excluded. The supplied proof slot is a placeholder; no completed proof is supplied.

submissions.explanation:
For every fixed real coefficient vector $c\in\mathbb R^n$, $0<p<1$,
$Q=\sum_jc_j^2>0$, and $t>0$, the claimed tail estimate is

$$
\Pr\{|H|>t\}\le
2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2(1-p)^2}{\Phi(p)Q}\right).
$$

**Notation and probability model.** Here $n\ge0$ is the number of coordinates,
$p$ is the drop probability, and $\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$ consists of independent
Bernoulli($p$) drop indicators $\omega_j$. A mask has mass
$w_p(\omega)=\prod_j[p\text{ if }\omega_j=1;\ 1-p\text{ otherwise}]$.
Set $q=1-p>0$ and
$H=\sum_j(c_j-(1-\omega_j)c_j/q)=q^{-1}\sum_jc_j(\omega_j-p)$.
The coefficient $\Phi(p)$ equals $(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ away from
$p=1/2$, and has the defined value $\Phi(1/2)=1/2$.

The proof multiplies the scalar Bernoulli exponential-moment bounds and
then applies the finite-sum Chernoff argument to both signs of the error.
Its scalar input is the proved theorem
[DAREx.KearnsSaulMGF](p2m:theorem/d384aa62-fd26-4739-9089-8a6a761e66f5),
which supplies $\Phi(p)>0$ and, for every real $u$,

$$
(1-p)e^{-up}+pe^{u(1-p)}\le e^{\Phi(p)u^2/4}.
$$

The solution proves the product factorization from the explicit finite mask
mass. Substituting $u_j=sc_j/q$ in the scalar bound gives, for every real $s$,

$$
\mathbb E e^{sH}
=\prod_j\left[(1-p)e^{-u_jp}+pe^{u_j(1-p)}\right]
\le\exp\left(\frac{\Phi(p)Q}{4q^2}s^2\right).
$$

All real scalar arguments are needed: the fixed coefficients may have either
sign. Independence is established by the finite product-sum identity; no
additional distributional hypothesis is introduced.

Put $a=\Phi(p)Q/(4q^2)>0$. For $s\ge0$, the pointwise implication
$H>t\Rightarrow e^{-st}e^{sH}\ge1$, multiplied by the nonnegative mask mass
and summed, gives

$$\Pr(H>t)\le e^{-st}\mathbb E e^{sH}\le e^{-st+as^2}.$$

Applying the same argument to $-H$ uses the already proved moment bound at
$-s$. Choose $s=t/(2a)>0$. The exponent becomes

$$-st+as^2=-\frac{t^2}{4a}=-\frac{t^2q^2}{\Phi(p)Q}.$$

Every mask in the strict event $t<|H|$ lies in $t<H$ or $t<-H$.
The solution proves the corresponding finite probability union bound and
adds the two equal exponential bounds. Masks at the threshold are excluded,
as required by the target. The positive-energy premise makes empty or zero
coefficient vectors vacuous; the defined midpoint value remains included.

**Formalization note.** This is a formal Lean bridge from the existing
source-backed scalar Kearns–Saul theorem to the DARE exponential-tail
milestone. The centered error identity, product moment bound, finite Chernoff
inequality, optimization, and two-sided union bound are proved in this file.
The scalar analytic theorem is proved by direct submission
`1c90041e-cee7-43e8-8dd8-35618782146f`; there are no remaining open
assumptions. Original tail sketch `905dd122-dc0e-4f71-8beb-2b89cb191db7`
became ACCEPTED when that scalar proof closed on 2026-09-29.
The top-level `theorem solution` matches the complete target type.
No new child nodes or strengthened target hypotheses are introduced.

**Sources.** Deng et al., *DARE the Extreme: Revisiting Delta-Parameter
Pruning For Fine-Tuned Models*, ICLR 2025,
[arXiv:2410.09344v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2), Appendix E.1,
PDF p. 29, Theorem E.1, equations (6)–(7); PDF p. 30, unnumbered tail display
immediately preceding equation (8); Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, equation (2).
The scalar input is Berend and Kontorovich, *On the Concentration of the
Missing Mass*, [arXiv:1210.3248v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1210.3248v1),
Section 3, PDF p. 3, Theorem 4, equation (6), with proof on PDF pp. 3–4.
Its one-sided Lemma 5 is not used for this absolute tail.

import Definitions.Def_DAREx_Model
import Theorems.Thm_DAREx_KearnsSaulMGF
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators
open DAREx

private lemma finite_chernoff {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≤ 1)
    (f : Mask n → ℝ) (t s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    probability p (fun ω ↦ t < f ω) ≤
      Real.exp (-s * t) * mean p (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (s * f ω)) := by
  classical
  unfold probability mean
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro ω _
  have hw := maskMass_nonneg hp hp' ω
  by_cases he : t < f ω
  · rw [if_pos he]
    have hexp : 1 ≤ Real.exp (-s * t) * Real.exp (s * f ω) := by
      rw [← Real.exp_add, ← Real.exp_zero]
      apply Real.exp_le_exp.2
      have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left he.le hs
      linarith
    calc
      maskMass p ω = maskMass p ω * 1 := by ring
      _ ≤ maskMass p ω * (Real.exp (-s * t) * Real.exp (s * f ω)) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hexp hw
      _ = Real.exp (-s * t) * (maskMass p ω * Real.exp (s * f ω)) := by ring
  · rw [if_neg he]
    exact mul_nonneg (Real.exp_pos _).le (mul_nonneg hw (Real.exp_pos _).le)

private lemma finite_absolute_union {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≤ 1)
    (f : Mask n → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    probability p (fun ω ↦ t < |f ω|) ≤
      probability p (fun ω ↦ t < f ω) + probability p (fun ω ↦ t < -f ω) := by
  classical
  unfold probability
  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro ω _
  have hw := maskMass_nonneg hp hp' ω
  by_cases hbad : t < |f ω|
  · rw [if_pos hbad]
    rcases lt_abs.1 hbad with hpos | hneg
    · rw [if_pos hpos]
      split_ifs <;> linarith
    · have hneg' : t < -f ω := by linarith
      rw [if_pos hneg']
      split_ifs <;> linarith
  · rw [if_neg hbad]
    split_ifs <;> linarith

private lemma finite_subgaussian_absolute_tail {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ)
    (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≤ 1) (f : Mask n → ℝ) (a t : ℝ)
    (ha : 0 < a) (ht : 0 < t)
    (hmgf : ∀ s : ℝ, mean p (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (s * f ω)) ≤
      Real.exp (a * s ^ 2)) :
    probability p (fun ω ↦ t < |f ω|) ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-(t ^ 2 / (4 * a))) := by
  let s := t / (2 * a)
  have hs : 0 < s := div_pos ht (mul_pos (by norm_num) ha)
  have hright : probability p (fun ω ↦ t < f ω) ≤
      Real.exp (-s * t) * Real.exp (a * s ^ 2) :=
    (finite_chernoff p hp hp' f t s hs.le).trans
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hmgf s) (Real.exp_pos _).le)
  have hleftmgf : mean p (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (s * -f ω)) ≤
      Real.exp (a * s ^ 2) := by
    simpa only [mul_neg, neg_mul, neg_sq] using hmgf (-s)
  have hleft : probability p (fun ω ↦ t < -f ω) ≤
      Real.exp (-s * t) * Real.exp (a * s ^ 2) :=
    (finite_chernoff p hp hp' (fun ω ↦ -f ω) t s hs.le).trans
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hleftmgf (Real.exp_pos _).le)
  have hopt : -s * t + a * s ^ 2 = -(t ^ 2 / (4 * a)) := by
    dsimp [s]
    field_simp
    ring
  have hsum := (finite_absolute_union p hp hp' f t).trans (add_le_add hright hleft)
  rw [← Real.exp_add, hopt] at hsum
  linarith

private lemma factorized_mgf {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ) (a : Fin n → Bool → ℝ) :
    mean p (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (∑ j, a j (ω j))) =
      ∏ j, ((1 - p) * Real.exp (a j false) + p * Real.exp (a j true)) := by
  unfold mean maskMass
  simp_rw [Real.exp_sum, ← Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
  simpa [add_comm] using (Fintype.prod_sum (fun (j : Fin n) (b : Bool) ↦
    (if b then p else 1 - p) * Real.exp (a j b))).symm

private lemma scaled_dareError {n : ℕ} (p s : ℝ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (hp : p < 1)
    (ω : Mask n) :
    s * dareError p c ω =
      ∑ j, (s * c j / (1 - p)) * ((if ω j then (1 : ℝ) else 0) - p) := by
  have hq : 1 - p ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt (sub_pos.mpr hp)
  unfold dareError outputError
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  cases hb : ω j <;> simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte]
  · field_simp
    ring
  · field_simp
    ring

private lemma dare_mgf_bound {n : ℕ} (p s : ℝ) (c : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p < 1)
    (hks : ∀ u : ℝ,
      (1 - p) * Real.exp (-u * p) + p * Real.exp (u * (1 - p)) ≤
        Real.exp (phi p * u ^ 2 / 4)) :
    mean p (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (s * dareError p c ω)) ≤
      Real.exp (phi p * energy c * s ^ 2 / (4 * (1 - p) ^ 2)) := by
  have hq : 0 < 1 - p := sub_pos.mpr hp'
  have hq' : 1 - p ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hq
  simp_rw [scaled_dareError p s c hp']
  rw [factorized_mgf p
    (fun j b ↦ (s * c j / (1 - p)) * ((if b then (1 : ℝ) else 0) - p))]
  simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte, zero_sub, mul_neg]
  calc
    _ ≤ ∏ j, Real.exp (phi p * (s * c j / (1 - p)) ^ 2 / 4) := by
      apply Finset.prod_le_prod
      · intro j _
        exact add_nonneg (mul_nonneg hq.le (Real.exp_pos _).le)
          (mul_nonneg hp.le (Real.exp_pos _).le)
      · intro j _
        simpa only [neg_mul] using hks (s * c j / (1 - p))
    _ = Real.exp (∑ j, phi p * (s * c j / (1 - p)) ^ 2 / 4) :=
      (Real.exp_sum _ _).symm
    _ = _ := by
      congr 1
      have hterm (j : Fin n) :
          phi p * (s * c j / (1 - p)) ^ 2 / 4 =
            (phi p * s ^ 2 / (4 * (1 - p) ^ 2)) * c j ^ 2 := by
        field_simp
      simp_rw [hterm]
      rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
      unfold energy
      ring

private lemma dare_tail_from_scalar {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p t : ℝ)
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p < 1) (hQ : 0 < energy c) (ht : 0 < t)
    (hphi : 0 < phi p)
    (hks : ∀ u : ℝ,
      (1 - p) * Real.exp (-u * p) + p * Real.exp (u * (1 - p)) ≤
        Real.exp (phi p * u ^ 2 / 4)) :
    probability p (fun ω ↦ t < |dareError p c ω|) ≤
      2 * Real.exp (-(t ^ 2 * (1 - p) ^ 2 / (phi p * energy c))) := by
  have hq : 0 < 1 - p := sub_pos.mpr hp'
  let a := phi p * energy c / (4 * (1 - p) ^ 2)
  have ha : 0 < a := div_pos (mul_pos hphi hQ)
    (mul_pos (by norm_num) (sq_pos_of_pos hq))
  have hmgf (s : ℝ) : mean p (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (s * dareError p c ω)) ≤
      Real.exp (a * s ^ 2) := by
    convert dare_mgf_bound p s c hp hp' hks using 1
    dsimp [a]
    congr 1
    ring
  have h := finite_subgaussian_absolute_tail p hp.le hp'.le (dareError p c) a t ha ht hmgf
  have hid : t ^ 2 / (4 * a) = t ^ 2 * (1 - p) ^ 2 / (phi p * energy c) := by
    dsimp [a]
    field_simp
  rw [hid] at h
  exact h

-- Deng et al., Appendix E.1, PDF p. 30, tail display preceding equation (8).
-- All finite-product and Chernoff steps are proved; only the scalar MGF is assumed.
theorem solution :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p t : ℝ),
      0 < p → p < 1 → 0 < energy c → 0 < t →
      probability p (fun ω ↦ t < |dareError p c ω|) ≤
        2 * Real.exp (-(t ^ 2 * (1 - p) ^ 2 / (phi p * energy c))) := by
  intro n c p t hp hp' hQ ht
  have hks := KearnsSaulMGF p hp hp'
  exact dare_tail_from_scalar c p t hp hp' hQ ht hks.1 hks.2.2

namespace DAREx
theorem DAREExponentialTail :
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p t : ℝ),
    0 < p → p < 1 → 0 < energy c → 0 < t →
    probability p (fun ω ↦ t < |dareError p c ω|) ≤
      2 * Real.exp (-(t ^ 2 * (1 - p) ^ 2 / (phi p * energy c))) := by sorry
end DAREx
theorem.natural_language_statement:
**Notation.** $\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$ is the finite space of Bernoulli drop masks; $n$ is the number of coordinates and $p$ is the drop probability. Coefficients are fixed before drawing the mask. Fix $n\ge0$, deterministic $c\in\mathbb R^n$, $0<p<1$, energy $Q=\sum_jc_j^2>0$, and $t>0$. Draw independent Bernoulli($p$) drop indicators and let $H=\sum_jc_j(1-(1-\omega_j)/(1-p))$. With $\Phi$ defined by the logarithmic quotient and $\Phi(1/2)=1/2$, $$\Pr(|H|>t)\le2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2(1-p)^2}{\Phi(p)Q}\right).$$ **Formalization note:** direct source tail formula with explicit positive energy for its denominator; strict $>t$ matches the source. Arbitrary signed coefficients are allowed. The main confidence-bound goal separately includes the zero-energy case.

**Source:** Deng et al., DARE the Extreme: Revisiting Delta-Parameter Pruning For Fine-Tuned Models, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.09344v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2, Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, equation (2); Appendix E.1, PDF p. 30, unnumbered tail display immediately preceding equation (8), from Theorem E.1, PDF p. 29, equations (6)–(7).

readback.readback: This open theorem asserts that, for every natural number $n$, every real coefficient family $c:I_n\to\mathbb R$ with $I_n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and every pair of real numbers $p,t$ satisfying $0<p<1$, $V:=\sum_{j\in I_n}c_j^2>0$, and $t>0$, one has $\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_n:\ t<|D(\omega)|}w_p(\omega)\le2\exp\!\bigl(-t^2(1-p)^2/(\phi(p)V)\bigr)$. Here $\Omega_n=\{\mathsf{false},\mathsf{true}\}^{I_n}$, $w_p(\omega)=\prod_{j\in I_n}a_p(\omega_j)$ with $a_p(\mathsf{true})=p$ and $a_p(\mathsf{false})=1-p$, so the left-hand side is the probability under the finite product distribution of independent Boolean coordinates each true with probability $p$; $D(\omega)=\sum_{j\in I_n}(c_j-h_j(\omega_j))$ with $h_j(\mathsf{true})=0$ and $h_j(\mathsf{false})=c_j/(1-p)$; and $\phi(p)=\tfrac12$ at $p=\tfrac12$ and $\phi(p)=(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ otherwise. Thus the error is a sum of $c_j$ on true coordinates and $c_j-c_j/(1-p)$ on false coordinates, with no subtraction of a separately introduced bias. The bad event is strictly $t<|D(\omega)|$, so masks with $|D(\omega)|=t$ are not counted. There are no sign or sum constraints on $c$, no upper bound on $t$, and no separately stated lower bound on $\phi(p)$; the only explicit energy hypothesis is $V>0$, which makes the premises unsatisfiable for $n=0$ or for the identically zero coefficient family. The size $n=1$ and all nonzero real coefficient families are otherwise included. The bound is the displayed exponential expression itself, with no truncation at $1$. submissions.explanation:
For every fixed real coefficient vector $c\in\mathbb R^n$, with $n>0$,
$0<p<1$, and $0<\gamma<1$, the claimed bound is

$$
\Pr\left\{|H|\le
\frac{\sqrt{\Phi(p)}}{1-p}
\sqrt{n(\bar c^2+\sigma^2)}\sqrt{\log(2/\gamma)}\right\}\ge1-\gamma.
$$

**Notation and probability model.** The sample space is
$\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$, with independent Bernoulli($p$) drop indicators
$\omega_j$. Thus $p$ is the drop probability and a mask has mass
$w_p(\omega)=\prod_j[p\text{ if }\omega_j=1;\ 1-p\text{ otherwise}]$.
Here $n$ is the number of coordinates, $\gamma$ is the failure allowance,
$H=\sum_j(c_j-(1-\omega_j)c_j/(1-p))$ is the DARE output error,
$Q=\sum_jc_j^2$, $\bar c=n^{-1}\sum_jc_j$, and
$\sigma^2=n^{-1}\sum_j(c_j-\bar c)^2$.
The function $\Phi$ is $(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ away from $p=1/2$,
with $\Phi(1/2)=1/2$.

The proof converts the existing exponential-tail theorem into a confidence
bound and handles zero energy directly. It uses the proved child
[DAREx.DAREExponentialTail](p2m:theorem/d7ac7bac-7a7c-4084-b4a8-4584aa769192),
which asserts, for $Q>0$ and $t>0$,

$$
\Pr\{|H|>t\}\le2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2(1-p)^2}{\Phi(p)Q}\right).
$$

The coefficient-energy identity is proved within the solution by expanding
the sum of squared deviations and using $n\bar c=\sum_jc_j$:

$$Q=n(\bar c^2+\sigma^2).$$

For $Q=0$, nonnegativity of every squared coefficient gives $c_j=0$ for
every $j$. Consequently $H=0$ for every mask and the radius is zero.
The good event contains every mask, so its probability is one by the
proved normalization of the product mass.

For $Q>0$, the solution proves $\Phi(p)>0$ directly. Below $1/2$, both
the numerator and logarithm in its definition are positive; above $1/2$,
both are negative; at $1/2$, the defined value is positive.
Also $1-p>0$ and $\log(2/\gamma)>0$. Therefore the radius

$$t=\frac{\sqrt{\Phi(p)}}{1-p}\sqrt Q\sqrt{\log(2/\gamma)}$$

is positive. Squaring the radius and cancelling positive denominators gives

$$\frac{t^2(1-p)^2}{\Phi(p)Q}=\log(2/\gamma),
\qquad 2\exp(-\log(2/\gamma))=\gamma.$$

The imported tail theorem thus bounds the bad-event probability by
$\gamma$. The events $|H|\le t$ and $t<|H|$ are complementary, including
masks whose error equals the radius. Their finite weighted probabilities
sum to one, which yields the required lower bound.

**Formalization note.** This is a formal Lean bridge from the existing
source-backed exponential-tail theorem to Appendix E.1 equation (8).
The energy identity, positivity, zero-energy case, and probability-complement
argument are proved in the submitted file; the analytic tail estimate is
supplied by its now-proved child, whose scalar Kearns–Saul input is also
proved. The full dependency chain has no open assumptions. The top-level
`theorem solution` has exactly the target type, with no additional hypotheses.
Original sketch `ec1ba3f1-a9c1-4311-9599-d4e6a473b07d` became ACCEPTED
when the scalar proof closed the chain on 2026-09-29.

**Source.** Deng et al., *DARE the Extreme: Revisiting Delta-Parameter
Pruning For Fine-Tuned Models*, ICLR 2025,
[arXiv:2410.09344v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2), Appendix E.1,

it; PDF p. 31, unnumbered coefficient-energy identity; Section 3.2,

open DAREx

private lemma concentration_energy_identity (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    energy c = (n : ℝ) * (empiricalMean c ^ 2 + empiricalVariance c) := by
  have hn' : (n : ℝ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.ne_of_gt hn)
  unfold empiricalVariance empiricalMean coefficientSum energy
  simp_rw [sub_sq, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_sub_distrib,
    ← Finset.sum_mul, ← Finset.mul_sum]
  simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
  field_simp
  ring

private lemma concentration_phi_pos {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p < 1) :
    0 < phi p := by
  unfold phi
  split_ifs with hhalf
  · norm_num
  · rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hhalf with hlow | hhigh
    · apply div_pos
      · linarith
      · apply Real.log_pos
        apply (lt_div_iff₀ hp).2
        linarith
    · apply div_pos_of_neg_of_neg
      · linarith
      · apply Real.log_neg
        · exact div_pos (sub_pos.mpr hp') hp
        · apply (div_lt_iff₀ hp).2
          linarith

private lemma concentration_probability_complement {n : ℕ} (p t : ℝ)
    (f : Mask n → ℝ) :
    probability p (fun ω ↦ |f ω| ≤ t) + probability p (fun ω ↦ t < |f ω|) = 1 := by
  classical
  unfold probability
  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← maskMass_sum (n := n) p]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro ω _
  by_cases h : |f ω| ≤ t
  · simp [h, not_lt.mpr h]
  · simp [h, lt_of_not_ge h]

private lemma concentration_energy_nonneg {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ energy c :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg (fun j _ ↦ sq_nonneg (c j))

private lemma concentration_zero_coefficients {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hQ : energy c = 0) : ∀ j, c j = 0 := by
  have hzero := (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg
    (fun j (_ : j ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))) ↦ sq_nonneg (c j))).1 hQ
  intro j
  exact (sq_eq_zero_iff).1 (hzero j (Finset.mem_univ j))

private lemma concentration_from_tail
    (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p γ : ℝ)
    (henergy : energy c = (n : ℝ) * (empiricalMean c ^ 2 + empiricalVariance c))
    (htail : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < energy c → 0 < t →
      probability p (fun ω ↦ t < |dareError p c ω|) ≤
        2 * Real.exp (-(t ^ 2 * (1 - p) ^ 2 / (phi p * energy c))))
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p < 1) (hγ : 0 < γ) (hγ' : γ < 1) :
    1 - γ ≤ probability p (fun ω ↦ |dareError p c ω| ≤
      Real.sqrt (phi p) / (1 - p) *
        Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) * (empiricalMean c ^ 2 + empiricalVariance c)) *
        Real.sqrt (Real.log (2 / γ))) := by
  classical
  rw [← henergy]
  by_cases hQ : energy c = 0
  · have hc := concentration_zero_coefficients c hQ
    have herror : ∀ ω : Mask n, dareError p c ω = 0 := by
      intro ω
      simp [dareError, outputError, hc]
    have hprob : probability p (fun ω ↦ |dareError p c ω| ≤
        Real.sqrt (phi p) / (1 - p) * Real.sqrt (energy c) *
          Real.sqrt (Real.log (2 / γ))) = 1 := by
      simp [probability, herror, hQ, maskMass_sum]
    rw [hprob]
    linarith
  · have hQpos : 0 < energy c := lt_of_le_of_ne (concentration_energy_nonneg c) (Ne.symm hQ)
    have hphi := concentration_phi_pos hp hp'
    have hden : 0 < 1 - p := sub_pos.mpr hp'
    have hlog : 0 < Real.log (2 / γ) := by
      apply Real.log_pos
      apply (lt_div_iff₀ hγ).2
      linarith
    let t := Real.sqrt (phi p) / (1 - p) * Real.sqrt (energy c) *
      Real.sqrt (Real.log (2 / γ))
    have ht : 0 < t := mul_pos
      (mul_pos (div_pos (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hphi) hden) (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hQpos))
      (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hlog)
    have hexponent : t ^ 2 * (1 - p) ^ 2 / (phi p * energy c) = Real.log (2 / γ) := by
      dsimp [t]
      rw [mul_pow, mul_pow, div_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hphi.le, Real.sq_sqrt hQpos.le,
        Real.sq_sqrt hlog.le]
      field_simp
    have hbound : 2 * Real.exp (-Real.log (2 / γ)) = γ := by
      rw [Real.exp_neg, Real.exp_log (div_pos (by norm_num) hγ)]
      field_simp
    have hbad : probability p (fun ω ↦ t < |dareError p c ω|) ≤ γ := by
      have h := htail t hQpos ht
      rw [hexponent, hbound] at h
      exact h
    have hcompl := concentration_probability_complement p t (dareError p c)
    change 1 - γ ≤ probability p (fun ω ↦ |dareError p c ω| ≤ t)
    linarith

-- Deng et al., Appendix E.1, PDF p. 30, equation (8), and PDF p. 31 energy identity.
-- The existing exponential-tail theorem is the only conditional dependency.
theorem solution :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p γ : ℝ),
      0 < n → 0 < p → p < 1 → 0 < γ → γ < 1 →
      1 - γ ≤ probability p (fun ω ↦ |dareError p c ω| ≤
        Real.sqrt (phi p) / (1 - p) *
          Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) * (empiricalMean c ^ 2 + empiricalVariance c)) *
          Real.sqrt (Real.log (2 / γ))) := by
  intro n c p γ hn hp hp' hγ hγ'
  exact concentration_from_tail n c p γ (concentration_energy_identity n c hn)
    (fun t hQ ht ↦ DAREExponentialTail n c p t hp hp' hQ ht) hp hp' hγ hγ'

namespace DAREx
theorem DAREOutputConcentration :
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p γ : ℝ),
    0 < n → 0 < p → p < 1 → 0 < γ → γ < 1 →
    1 - γ ≤ probability p (fun ω ↦ |dareError p c ω| ≤
      Real.sqrt (phi p) / (1 - p) *
        Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) * (empiricalMean c ^ 2 + empiricalVariance c)) *
        Real.sqrt (Real.log (2 / γ))) := by sorry
end DAREx
theorem.natural_language_statement:
**Notation.** $\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$ is the finite space of Bernoulli drop masks; $n$ is the number of coordinates and $p$ is the drop probability. Coefficients are fixed before drawing the mask. For $n>0$, fix any real influence coefficients $c_j=\Delta W_jx_j$. Set $\bar c=n^{-1}\sum_jc_j$ and $\sigma^2=n^{-1}\sum_j(c_j-\bar c)^2$. Let $0<p<1$ be the drop probability and $0<\gamma<1$ the allowed failure probability. Draw independent Bernoulli($p$) drop indicators $\omega_j$ and define $H=\sum_jc_j(1-(1-\omega_j)/(1-p))$. Put $\Phi(1/2)=1/2$ and $\Phi(p)=(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ otherwise. Then $$\Pr\left\{|H|\le\frac{\sqrt{\Phi(p)}}{1-p}\sqrt{n(\bar c^2+\sigma^2)}\sqrt{\log(2/\gamma)}\right\}\ge1-\gamma.$$ There is no nonzero-coefficient or positive-energy hypothesis. **Formalization note:** equation (8), using the source's coefficient-energy identity, with an explicit continuous value at $p=1/2$. This is not the piecewise formula printed in Theorem 3.1: the missing square root and the one-sided high-pruning refinement are not imported. The mission description explains the distinction.

**Source:** Deng et al., DARE the Extreme: Revisiting Delta-Parameter Pruning For Fine-Tuned Models, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.09344v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2, Appendix E.1, PDF p. 30, equation (8); PDF p. 31, unnumbered coefficient-energy identity; Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, equation (2) and Theorem 3.1 notation.

readback.readback: This open theorem asserts that, for every natural number $n$, every real coefficient family $c:I_n\to\mathbb R$ with $I_n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and every pair of real numbers $p,\gamma$ satisfying $0<n$, $0<p<1$, and $0<\gamma<1$, one has $1-\gamma\le\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_n:\ |D(\omega)|\le R}w_p(\omega)$, where $R=\dfrac{\sqrt{\phi(p)}}{1-p}\sqrt{n(\bar c^{\,2}+s_c^2)}\sqrt{\log(2/\gamma)}$, $\bar c=(\sum_{j\in I_n}c_j)/n$, and $s_c^2=(\sum_{j\in I_n}(c_j-\bar c)^2)/n$. The natural number $n$ is interpreted as a real number in these formulas and the variance uses denominator $n$, not $n-1$. Here $\Omega_n=\{\mathsf{false},\mathsf{true}\}^{I_n}$, $w_p(\omega)=\prod_{j\in I_n}a_p(\omega_j)$ with $a_p(\mathsf{true})=p$ and $a_p(\mathsf{false})=1-p$, so the sum is the probability for independent Boolean coordinates each true with probability $p$; $D(\omega)=\sum_{j\in I_n}(c_j-h_j(\omega_j))$, where $h_j(\mathsf{true})=0$ and $h_j(\mathsf{false})=c_j/(1-p)$; and $\phi(p)=\tfrac12$ if $p=\tfrac12$, otherwise $\phi(p)=(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$. The square roots are real square roots, with the total convention that a nonpositive input has square root $0$. The good event uses the weak inequality $|D(\omega)|\le R$ and is centered at error $0$. There is no positivity assumption on $\sum_jc_j^2$, no separate assumption about $\phi(p)$, and no sign or nonzero restriction on the coefficients. In particular, the identically zero coefficient family is included: then $D=R=0$ and the event contains every mask. The case $n=0$ is excluded, but $n=1$ is included and has $s_c^2=0$; both endpoints of each interval for $p$ and $\gamma$ are excluded. The supplied proof slot is a placeholder; no completed proof is supplied.

namespace DAREx
theorem DAREExponentialTail :
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p t : ℝ),
    0 < p → p < 1 → 0 < energy c → 0 < t →
    probability p (fun ω ↦ t < |dareError p c ω|) ≤
      2 * Real.exp (-(t ^ 2 * (1 - p) ^ 2 / (phi p * energy c))) := by sorry
end DAREx
theorems.natural_language_statement:
**Notation.** $\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$ is the finite space of Bernoulli drop masks; $n$ is the number of coordinates and $p$ is the drop probability. Coefficients are fixed before drawing the mask. Fix $n\ge0$, deterministic $c\in\mathbb R^n$, $0<p<1$, energy $Q=\sum_jc_j^2>0$, and $t>0$. Draw independent Bernoulli($p$) drop indicators and let $H=\sum_jc_j(1-(1-\omega_j)/(1-p))$. With $\Phi$ defined by the logarithmic quotient and $\Phi(1/2)=1/2$, $$\Pr(|H|>t)\le2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2(1-p)^2}{\Phi(p)Q}\right).$$ **Formalization note:** direct source tail formula with explicit positive energy for its denominator; strict $>t$ matches the source. Arbitrary signed coefficients are allowed. The main confidence-bound goal separately includes the zero-energy case.

**Source:** Deng et al., DARE the Extreme: Revisiting Delta-Parameter Pruning For Fine-Tuned Models, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.09344v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2, Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, equation (2); Appendix E.1, PDF p. 30, unnumbered tail display immediately preceding equation (8), from Theorem E.1, PDF p. 29, equations (6)–(7).

namespace DAREx
theorem KearnsSaulMGF :
  ∀ p : ℝ, 0 < p → p < 1 →
    0 < phi p ∧ phi p ≤ 1 / 2 ∧
    ∀ t : ℝ, (1 - p) * Real.exp (-t * p) + p * Real.exp (t * (1 - p)) ≤
      Real.exp (phi p * t ^ 2 / 4) := by sorry
end DAREx
theorems.natural_language_statement:
**Notation.** $B$ is a Bernoulli random variable, $p=\Pr(B=1)$, $t$ is an arbitrary real exponential-moment parameter, and $\Phi$ is defined below. For $0<p<1$, let $\Phi(p)=(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ when $p\ne1/2$, and $\Phi(1/2)=1/2$. Then $0<\Phi(p)\le1/2$, and for every real $t$, $$ (1-p)e^{-tp}+pe^{t(1-p)}\le\exp(\Phi(p)t^2/4).$$ The left side is the exponential moment of a centered Bernoulli($p$) variable. Both signs of $t$ are part of the conclusion. **Formalization note:** explicitly sourced external analytic input, specialized to the open probability interval needed by DARE, together with the source's coefficient bound. The half-probability value is the removable-singularity extension in the proof of Berend–Kontorovich Theorem 4. It is not the one-sided refinement in Lemma 5.

namespace DAREx
theorem RescaledErrorMoments :
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (p q : ℝ), 0 ≤ p → p ≤ 1 → 0 < q →
    mean p (outputError q c) = outputBias p q c ∧
    mean p (fun ω ↦ (outputError q c ω - outputBias p q c) ^ 2) =
      p * (1 - p) / q ^ 2 * energy c ∧
    mean p (fun ω ↦ outputError q c ω ^ 2) =
      outputBias p q c ^ 2 + p * (1 - p) / q ^ 2 * energy c := by sorry
end DAREx
theorems.natural_language_statement:
**Notation.** $\Omega=\{0,1\}^n$ is the finite space of Bernoulli drop masks; $n$ is the number of coordinates and $p$ is the drop probability. Coefficients are fixed before drawing the mask. For any $n\ge0$, fixed coefficients $c_j\in\mathbb R$, $0\le p\le1$, and $q>0$, draw independent Bernoulli($p$) drop indicators $\omega_j$. Put $H_q=\sum_jc_j(1-(1-\omega_j)/q)$, $S=\sum_jc_j$, $Q=\sum_jc_j^2$, and $b_q=(1-(1-p)/q)S$. Then $$\mathbb EH_q=b_q,\qquad\mathbb E(H_q-b_q)^2=\frac{p(1-p)}{q^2}Q,$$ $$\mathbb EH_q^2=b_q^2+\frac{p(1-p)}{q^2}Q.$$ Expectations are finite product-mask sums. **Formalization note:** paper-derived extension of the DARE moment calculation to the general $1/q$ rescaling model; this does not assert the optimizer or tail formula later printed in Appendix E.2. Empty vectors and deterministic endpoint masks are included.

**Source:** Deng et al., DARE the Extreme: Revisiting Delta-Parameter Pruning For Fine-Tuned Models, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.09344v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.09344v2, Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, equation (2); Appendix E.1, PDF p. 29, initial unnumbered mean/variance calculations; Appendix E.2, PDF p. 31, initial unnumbered general-rescaling identity.

theorem CoefficientEnergyIdentity :
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℝ), 0 < n →
    energy c = (n : ℝ) * (empiricalMean c ^ 2 + empiricalVariance c) := by sorry

**Notation.** The fixed-cardinality coordinate set is $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with $n=|I|$; $c_j$ are real coefficients, $Q$ their squared energy, and $\bar c,\sigma^2$ their empirical statistics. For $n>0$ and any deterministic real coefficient vector $c\in\mathbb R^n$, define $Q=\sum_jc_j^2$, $\bar c=n^{-1}\sum_jc_j$, and $\sigma^2=n^{-1}\sum_j(c_j-\bar c)^2$. Then $$Q=n(\bar c^2+\sigma^2).$$ These are statistics over coordinates, not moments over random pruning. **Formalization note:** direct algebraic identity used in the source; no coefficient sign assumption.

theorems.definition:
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Ring.Finset
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real

noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators

namespace DAREx

/-- A true bit denotes a dropped coordinate. -/
abbrev Mask (n : ℕ) := Fin n → Bool

/-- Product law of independent Bernoulli drop indicators. -/
def maskMass {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ) (ω : Mask n) : ℝ :=
  ∏ j, if ω j then p else 1 - p

def mean {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ) (f : Mask n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ ω, maskMass p ω * f ω

def probability {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ) (event : Mask n → Prop) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact ∑ ω, if event ω then maskMass p ω else 0

def coefficientSum {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ j, c j

def energy {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ j, c j ^ 2

def empiricalMean {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ := coefficientSum c / n

def empiricalVariance {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j, (c j - empiricalMean c) ^ 2) / n

/-- Original output minus pruned output, with surviving weights rescaled by `1/q`. -/
def outputError {n : ℕ} (q : ℝ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) (ω : Mask n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j, (c j - (if ω j then 0 else c j / q))

def dareError {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) : Mask n → ℝ :=
  outputError (1 - p) c

def outputBias {n : ℕ} (p q : ℝ) (c : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (1 - (1 - p) / q) * coefficientSum c

/-- Continuous value at one half; analytic claims use `0 < p < 1`. -/
def phi (p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if p = 1 / 2 then 1 / 2 else (1 - 2 * p) / Real.log ((1 - p) / p)

lemma maskMass_nonneg {n : ℕ} {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≤ 1) (ω : Mask n) :
    0 ≤ maskMass p ω := by
  apply Finset.prod_nonneg
  intro j _
  split
  · exact hp
  · exact sub_nonneg.mpr hp'

lemma maskMass_sum {n : ℕ} (p : ℝ) : ∑ ω : Mask n, maskMass p ω = 1 := by
  unfold maskMass
  simpa using (Fintype.prod_sum (fun (_ : Fin n) (b : Bool) ↦
    if b then p else 1 - p)).symm

end DAREx
theorems.natural_language_statement:
Fix a natural number $n$ and deterministic real coefficients $c_j$, indexed by $j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. A Boolean mask $\omega$ records dropped coordinates. For $0\le p\le1$, it has mass $w_p(\omega)=\prod_j[p\text{ if }\omega_j=1;\;1-p\text{ otherwise}]$, so the drops are independent Bernoulli variables of parameter $p$. The bundle defines expectation and event probability as the finite weighted sums and proves nonnegative masses and total mass one.

Write $S=\sum_jc_j$, $Q=\sum_jc_j^2$, $\bar c=S/n$, and $\sigma^2=n^{-1}\sum_j(c_j-\bar c)^2$. The statistical identities using these last two quantities require $n>0$. For a positive rescaling denominator $q$, set $H_q(\omega)=\sum_jc_j(1-(1-\omega_j)/q)$ and $b_q=(1-(1-p)/q)S$. DARE uses $H=H_{1-p}$ for $0<p<1$. Define $\Phi(1/2)=1/2$ and $\Phi(p)=(1-2p)/\log((1-p)/p)$ otherwise; concentration theorems restrict $p$ to $(0,1)$.

**Formalization note.** Finite-sum encoding of the paper's Bernoulli probability model: true means dropped, the complement of its retention variable. Definitions are total Lean functions; no probability or analytic claim is made outside the stated domains. The model is not an assumption of any concentration conclusion. Primary reference: Deng et al., Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, equation (2); Appendix E.1, PDF pp. 29–31, equations (7)–(8); Appendix E.2, PDF p. 31, initial unnumbered identity. See the linked source.

import Mathlib

/-!
# Normalization in the plane tropical Bézout formula

For the standard lattice triangle dilated by a natural degree `d`, normalized
lattice area is `d²` when the primitive lattice triangle has area one.  This
file computes the corresponding polarization exactly.  The result exposes a
factor of two: the raw difference of normalized areas is `2de`, whereas the
Bézout intersection number is `de`.
-/

namespace TropicalMixedArea

/-- Normalized lattice area of the degree-`d` standard Newton triangle. -/
def normalizedTriangleArea (d : ℕ) : ℤ := (d : ℤ) ^ 2

/-- The raw area polarization for two standard Newton triangles. -/
def normalizedMixedAreaDifference (d e : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  normalizedTriangleArea (d + e) - normalizedTriangleArea d -
    normalizedTriangleArea e







end TropicalMixedArea

/-!
# Comparison estimates for ideal triangles under variable curvature

The previous files work at *constant* curvature `-κ`, where the area element is
`dx dy / (κ y²)`.  Here we allow the curvature to vary — the area element
becomes `dx dy / (K(x) y²)` for a positive function `K` — and prove the
expected comparison inequalities:

`κ₁ ≤ K ≤ κ₂  ⟹  π / κ₂ ≤ area ≤ π / κ₁`.

In words: *pinching the curvature between `-κ₂` and `-κ₁` pinches the area of an
ideal triangle between `π/κ₂` and `π/κ₁`*, and more negative curvature means a
smaller ideal triangle.  At `K` constant both bounds collapse to the exact value
`π / κ` of `idealTriangleArea_eq`, so the comparison theorem is sharp.

## Main results

* `variableSlicedArea_eq`:  slicing formula in the variable-curvature setting
  (no hypothesis on `K` is needed).
* `variableSlicedArea_le_of_le` / `le_variableSlicedArea_of_le`:  the two
  comparison inequalities.
* `variableSlicedArea_pinched`:  the two-sided pinching statement.
* `variableSlicedArea_const`:  sharpness — for constant curvature the bounds are
  attained.
-/

import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_Geometry_CosmicHorror_HyperbolicIdealArea
import Definitions.Def_Geometry_CosmicHorror_IdealTriangle

/-!
# From angle data to a Riemannian area integral: ideal triangles in the half-plane

The companion file `Geometry/CosmicHorror/IdealTriangle.lean` studies the
*algebraic* Gauss–Bonnet invariant

`hyperbolicArea κ α β γ = (π - (α + β + γ)) / κ`

as a function of angle data only.  The present file replaces the angle data by
an honest Riemannian computation in the **upper half-plane model** of the
hyperbolic plane of constant curvature `-κ`, whose area element is

`dA = dx dy / (κ y²)`.

## Main results

* `hasDerivAt_arcsinChord` / `intervalIntegrable_invSqrtChord`:  the analytic
  core, an explicit antiderivative for the chordal density
  `x ↦ (√((x - a)(b - x)))⁻¹` together with its (improper) integrability.
* `integral_invSqrtChord`:  `∫ x in a..b, (√((x - a)(b - x)))⁻¹ = π`.
  This is the whole geometry of an ideal triangle compressed into one identity.
* `integral_Ioi_inv_sq`:  the vertical fibre integral `∫_{c}^{∞} y⁻² dy = c⁻¹`,
  i.e. the hyperbolic length of the fibre measure above a point.
* `idealTriangleArea_eq`:  **the area of the ideal triangle with vertices
  `a < b` on the real line and `∞` equals `π / κ`**, computed from the area
  element by Fubini-style slicing.  Together with
  `idealTriangleArea_eq_hyperbolicArea` this *derives* the value that
  `IdealTriangle.lean` obtained from Gauss–Bonnet with all angles `0`.
* `idealPolygonArea_eq`:  the ideal `(m+2)`-gon with finite vertices
  `v 0 < ⋯ < v m` and last vertex `∞` has area `m · π / κ = ((n - 2) π)/κ`.
* `truncatedIdealTriangleArea_lt` and `tendsto_truncatedIdealTriangleArea`:
  the degeneration statement — the compact exhaustion of an ideal triangle by
  truncated regions has strictly smaller area, converging to `π / κ`.
* `angles_tendsto_zero_of_area_tendsto_max`:  conversely, on the angle side, a
  sequence of admissible triangles whose Gauss–Bonnet area tends to the maximum
  `π / κ` must have *all three* angles tending to `0`; the ideal triangle is the
  unique limiting shape.
-/

/-! ### Supporting helper — interior points are not extreme

An interior point of any set in `ℝ²` cannot be an extreme point: it is the
midpoint of two distinct nearby points of the set (obtained from a ball inside
the interior), so it is a non-trivial convex combination, contradicting the
extreme-point definition. -/



/-! ### §3.2 — `arcAngle` injective on `A` for an interior center

If `c` is interior to `convexHull A`, two distinct convex-independent points of
`A` cannot share a ray from `c`: the nearer one would be a strictly interior
point of the hull, contradicting convex independence. We package this through a
sequence of standard convexity facts: a Hahn-Banach "descent" lemma, the
extreme-point characterization of the hull, and the interior/extreme
incompatibility above. The injectivity statement lives on `Real.Angle` (not
`.toReal`), as required by the cut-open enumeration in §3.4. -/













/-! ### §3.3 / §3.4 — cut-open linear key and the sorted enumeration -/







/-! ### §3.5 sub-lemma A — sign of an arc-angle difference from the clockwise gap

Two arc-angles `a, b : Real.Angle` differ by `b - a = ↑(b.toReal - a.toReal)`, whose
`Real.Angle.sign` is `SignType.sign (Real.sin (b.toReal - a.toReal))`. The cut-open key
`cutKey θ = -θ.toReal` is strictly increasing along the enumeration, so for `i < j` the
`toReal`s are strictly *decreasing*: `θ_j.toReal < θ_i.toReal`, i.e. the clockwise gap
`g := θ_j.toReal - θ_i.toReal` is negative. The sign of `(θ_j - θ_i)` is then governed by
whether the clockwise gap exceeds `π` in magnitude:

* `g ∈ (-π, 0)` (gap `< π`) ⇒ sign `-1`;
* `g ∈ (-2π, -π)` (gap `> π`) ⇒ sign `+1`. -/

/-! ### §3.5 sub-lemma B — interior center is "surrounded" by `A`

If `c` is interior to `convexHull A`, no closed half-plane through `c` contains all of `A`:
for every nonzero direction `u`, some `a ∈ A` has `⟪a - c, u⟫ < 0`. Proved by the §3.2
Hahn-Banach idiom in reverse — the closed half-space `{x | ⟪c,u⟫ ≤ ⟪x,u⟫}` is convex and
(if it contained all of `A`) would contain the whole hull, but a ball around the interior
point `c` pokes out of it in the `-u` direction. -/



/-! ### §3.5 sub-lemma D — center-apex chord chirality from the clockwise gap

Packages Bridge 2 (`signedArea2_center_sign_eq_arcAngle_sub_sign`) with sub-lemma A: the
center-apex signed area `signedArea2 c a b` is negative exactly when the clockwise gap
`arcAngle c b - arcAngle c a` is a "short" turn (its `toReal`-representative lies in
`(-π, 0)`), and positive on a "long" turn (`(-2π, -π)`). -/

/-! ### Supporting helper — interior points are not extreme

An interior point of any set in `ℝ²` cannot be an extreme point: it is the
midpoint of two distinct nearby points of the set (obtained from a ball inside
the interior), so it is a non-trivial convex combination, contradicting the
extreme-point definition. -/



/-! ### §3.2 — `arcAngle` injective on `A` for an interior center

If `c` is interior to `convexHull A`, two distinct convex-independent points of
`A` cannot share a ray from `c`: the nearer one would be a strictly interior
point of the hull, contradicting convex independence. We package this through a
sequence of standard convexity facts: a Hahn-Banach "descent" lemma, the
extreme-point characterization of the hull, and the interior/extreme
incompatibility above. The injectivity statement lives on `Real.Angle` (not
`.toReal`), as required by the cut-open enumeration in §3.4. -/













/-! ### §3.3 / §3.4 — cut-open linear key and the sorted enumeration -/







/-! ### §3.5 sub-lemma A — sign of an arc-angle difference from the clockwise gap

Two arc-angles `a, b : Real.Angle` differ by `b - a = ↑(b.toReal - a.toReal)`, whose
`Real.Angle.sign` is `SignType.sign (Real.sin (b.toReal - a.toReal))`. The cut-open key
`cutKey θ = -θ.toReal` is strictly increasing along the enumeration, so for `i < j` the
`toReal`s are strictly *decreasing*: `θ_j.toReal < θ_i.toReal`, i.e. the clockwise gap
`g := θ_j.toReal - θ_i.toReal` is negative. The sign of `(θ_j - θ_i)` is then governed by
whether the clockwise gap exceeds `π` in magnitude:

* `g ∈ (-π, 0)` (gap `< π`) ⇒ sign `-1`;
* `g ∈ (-2π, -π)` (gap `> π`) ⇒ sign `+1`. -/

/-! ### §3.5 sub-lemma B — interior center is "surrounded" by `A`

If `c` is interior to `convexHull A`, no closed half-plane through `c` contains all of `A`:
for every nonzero direction `u`, some `a ∈ A` has `⟪a - c, u⟫ < 0`. Proved by the §3.2
Hahn-Banach idiom in reverse — the closed half-space `{x | ⟪c,u⟫ ≤ ⟪x,u⟫}` is convex and
(if it contained all of `A`) would contain the whole hull, but a ball around the interior
point `c` pokes out of it in the `-u` direction. -/

Packages Bridge 2 (`signedArea2_center_sign_eq_arcAngle_sub_sign`) with sub-lemma A: the
center-apex signed area `signedArea2 c a b` is negative exactly when the clockwise gap
`arcAngle c b - arcAngle c a` is a "short" turn (its `toReal`-representative lies in
`(-π, 0)`), and positive on a "long" turn (`(-2π, -π)`). -/

/-!
# Moser triangle vertices are noncollinear: nonzero signed area

The circumscribed branch of `Problem97.MEC.MoserTriangle` carries three
pairwise distinct `A`-vertices on the MEC boundary. This file proves that
those three vertices have nonzero `signedArea2`, which the downstream
cap-partition consumer (`Problem97.MEC.cap_partition_from_moser_circumscribed`)
needs to discharge its `hMoserNonDeg` hypothesis.

## Mathematical content

Three distinct points equidistant from a common center cannot be
collinear: a line meets a circle in at most two points. We package
this via Mathlib's strict-convex-space machinery:

* If three collinear points lie on a circle, one is `Wbtw` of the other
  two by `Collinear.wbtw_or_wbtw_or_wbtw`. With pairwise distinctness
  this strengthens to `Sbtw`, and `Sbtw.dist_lt_max_dist` gives a
  strictly smaller distance to the center — contradicting equidistance.

To translate to `signedArea2`, we prove
`signedArea2 v1 v2 v3 = 0 → Collinear ℝ {v1, v2, v3}` directly from the
2D cross-product identity (case analysis on which coordinate of
`v2 - v1` is nonzero, picking the scalar accordingly).

## Main declarations

* `Problem97.collinear_of_signedArea2_eq_zero` — algebraic predicate
  `signedArea2 = 0` implies the three points are collinear.
* `Problem97.MEC.not_collinear_of_three_dist_eq` — three distinct
  equidistant points are noncollinear (uses `StrictConvexSpace ℝ ℝ²`).
* `Problem97.MEC.signedArea2_ne_zero_of_three_dist_eq` — combining the
  two: three distinct equidistant points have nonzero signed area.
* `Problem97.MEC.moser_triangle_signed_area_ne_zero` — the target
  theorem applied to the circumscribed branch of `MoserTriangle`.

/-!
# Circumcenter-side characterization for non-obtuse inscribed triangles

Three points `a, b, c` on a Euclidean sphere of center `O` form a non-obtuse
triangle iff the smallest enclosing disk of `{a, b, c}` is the sphere itself.
Geometrically this puts the circumcenter `O` inside (or on the boundary of)
the triangle, which downstream consumers use through the signed-area form:
for each chord (say `ab`), the third vertex `c` and the center `O` lie on
the same closed half-plane.

The forward direction is captured by `center_same_side_as_apex_of_nonobtuse`:
if the interior angle of the triangle at `c` is non-obtuse — i.e.,
`⟪a - c, b - c⟫_ℝ ≥ 0` — then `signedArea2 O a b * signedArea2 c a b ≥ 0`.

The proof reduces to a single algebraic identity. With
`m := midpoint ℝ a b` and assuming the perpendicular-bisector condition
`‖a - O‖ = ‖b - O‖` (automatic from the sphere hypothesis):

  `signedArea2 O a b * signedArea2 c a b
      = ⟪m - O, m - c⟫_ℝ * ‖a - b‖²`.

The right-hand side is the product of a sphere-shaped quantity that the
inscribed-angle lemma `inner_chord_eq_two_mul_inner_midpoint` converts to
`(1/2) · ⟪a - c, b - c⟫_ℝ`, and a manifestly non-negative scalar `‖a - b‖²`.
Together with the hypothesis `⟪a - c, b - c⟫_ℝ ≥ 0`, this gives the result.

The companion `signedArea_prod_eq_inner_mul_dist_sq` is the abstract identity
without the inner-product hypothesis on `c`; it depends only on the
perpendicular-bisector condition on `O`. We also expose a `‖·‖²` form
(`signedArea_prod_eq_inner_mul_dist_sq`) that is more convenient for direct
algebraic chaining than re-deriving it from scratch.
-/
